content: Initial plan for agent-scoping: opens with the roadmap-gated project-model decision checkpoint (adoption trial opened 2026-07-11, so unless the human states otherwise this records 'insufficient evidence — deferred; soft domain tags remain pending trial data' in adoption log + decision log; the auth work proceeds either way). AgentKey model (name slug, sha256 key_hash, default_domain, allowed_domains superset containing default, is_active, last_used_at; egk_ prefixed secrets shown once). Three principal classes: owner (global key/session — unchanged full visibility), agent (enforced), anonymous (dev open mode — unchanged; zero AgentKey rows == today's behavior, hard-tested). Agent enforcement identical on REST and MCP via one shared core/services/scoping.py module: write injection of default domain / explicit rejection of out-of-allowed domains (never silent rewrite); scoped reads default-constrained to default_domain with explicit selection of other allowed domains; formerly-unscoped surfaces closed for agents (detail/update/delete 404-not-403 no-existence-oracle, stats/tags/list_domains restricted to allowed unions, untagged memories invisible to agents, owner sees all). MCP custom TokenVerifier (global key -> owner, agent key -> claims) with FastMCP access-token dependency. Live verify: two keys, different domains, cross-invisibility on every surface. Plan at docs/phases/agent-scoping.md.

Approved. The plan is consistent with the current REST/MCP auth surfaces, keeps owner and anonymous behavior explicit, and correctly scopes the first deliverable around the adoption-log / decision-log checkpoint before implementation lands.
